Published online:
    August 28, 2025 (Reuters, Orlando)
Geographic focus:
    United States
Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — extensive context on Fed communication evolution from Greenspan through Bernanke
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Warsh's communication overhaul and immediate market volatility risk
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — inflation anchoring, term premium, potential rate hikes

Synopsis:
    The article examines Kevin Warsh's push to overhaul Fed communication strategy, arguing the Bernanke-era model of maximum transparency and forward guidance has overshot. Warsh wants a "quieter Fed," fewer speeches, less spoon-feeding of markets. The piece is critical: inflation has been above 2% for 5.5+ years, the fed funds rate has been cut 175bps since the last hike, and the gap between Fed rhetoric and reality has widened. Long yields and term premiums are near 12-year highs. Warsh's own communication track record is already being panned (post-July press conference). The core risk: pulling back on signaling creates a vacuum that uncertainty and volatility will fill, potentially keeping risk premia elevated precisely when the Fed may need credibility to tighten.

Relevance: YES — the piece is centrally about Fed communication, its impact on yields, inflation expectations, and the interest rate path

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: +45 (meaningfully hawkish lean — sticky inflation above target for 5.5 years, term premium near 12-year highs, article explicitly states the Fed will "likely have to raise rates," Warsh's credibility concerns adding upward pressure on risk premia; net direction tilts hawkish despite current policy paralysis)
